title: Source adaptation gave uncertain 50 Hz prediction gains in three selected Allen slice groups
abstract: We tested whether source firing adaptation improves prediction of 50 Hz synaptic response change in Allen r2.1 slices. Donor-held-out ridge models controlled cell labels, distance, initial response size, and trial count. Primary mean absolute error gains were -0.00134 in 155 mouse excitatory connections, -0.00053 in 345 mouse inhibitory connections, and 0.01938 in 76 human excitatory connections. All conditional 98.75% donor bootstrap intervals included zero. An alternate donor split gave a positive human excitatory interval, so that result depends on the split. Eight human inhibitory connections were too few to test. Independent scoring and strong synthetic-signal checks passed. Selected slices, missing measurements, different time scales, and limited human donors prevent causal or cross-species conclusions. Original code, aggregate results, hashes, and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records stay outside the publication.
